messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx errors observed for service redwood-prod behind ELB prod-elb-us-west-2. 5xx rate ~11.8% over baseline in last 3m. Route53 health checks for us-west-2 failing intermittently. Paging: @Maria
Maria: ACK. taking lead.
Maria: pulling ELB target health + CW metrics now
Sam: grabbing ELB access logs and k8s node statuses
Raj: checking Route53 query logs + health-check config (TTL/interval). any recent DNS changes?
Maria: ELB target-group shows many targets UNHEALTHY in us-west-2a/us-west-2c with 502/503. kube-probe timeouts on some pods. sample from access log:
```
2026-03-21T04:12:10.123Z GET /v1/stream 502 34 "-" "python-requests/2.28" target=10.2.14.9:8080
```
Maria: ssh to node 10.2.14.9 times out intermittently. ping loss ~40% to node IPs.
Sam: EBS gp3 volume metrics show io_stall spikes on subset of instances in az-c (iowait ~6000ms). Could be host-level network congestion affecting EBS -> app errors
Raj: Route53 resolver latency from our VPCs in us-west-2 spikes 100-700ms tails. Health-checks flip between OK/FAIL rapidly. We have weighted records that prefer us-west-2 for certain customers which explains flapping observed by clients
Irene: EC2 host status checks show some degraded reachability in az-c. AWS console reports "Impaired network connectivity" for a handful of hosts.
Kevin: Opening AWS support case now. Case# 9876543210 (EC2/ELB/Route53). AWS initial reply: investigating degraded network fabric in us-west-2 AZ-c.
Maria: Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce weight for us-west-2 in Route53 weighted set to 10% (shift traffic to us-west-1 and eu-west-1 where appropriate) 2) mark affected ELB targets as draining to allow healthy nodes to serve 3) apply short client-side retry/backoff suggestions to SDKs 4) enable api-gateway throttling to protect backend while we shift
Sam: deploying throttling rule to api-gateway staging and prod now (60rps burst 120)
Raj: submitting change to Route53 with TTL 30s. command used:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z0ABC --change-batch file://route53-shift-usw1.json
```
SupportBot: Notifying high-touch customers (acct: 121, 304, 882) with impacted endpoints and workaround guidance (redirect to alternate region). template link: https://intra.redwood/support/templates/usw2-outage
Maria: Route53 changes propagated; traffic to us-west-2 decreased ~68% over last 90s. 5xx rate dropped from 11.8% -> 2.6% after shift + throttling. ELB target health stabilizing on nodes in us-west-1
Kevin: Handing oncall to @Kevin (SRE lead). Maria keep monitoring AWS case and ELB target group trends. If degraded >30m prepare DR runbook for cross-region failover (notify product & sales)
Maria: Handoff: current state: traffic shifted, error rate reduced, AWS assigned an engineer. I'll continue until AWS provides RCA or we fully recover.
Kevin: Assigning postmortem owner @Irene. Capture timeline, impacted customers, changes to DNS health-checks, and followups (increase health-check interval, review weighted-record TTLs, add automated region-evacuation runbook).
Irene: Will create initial postmortem doc and link here. ETA 24h for first draft.
IncidentBot: If no regression for 45m mark RECOVERED and start RCA phase
Maria: marking stabilized. we'll keep elevated watch for 2h. Adding notes: suspected root cause = AZ-c network fabric degradation causing EBS/EC2 reachability problems -> backend failures -> ELB health-check flapping -> DNS weighted routing churn amplified client failover.
Maria: final ops summary: Partial AZ networking degradation in us-west-2 (az-c) caused ELB target failures and Route53 health check instability. Mitigations: regional traffic shift via weighted DNS, API throttling, ELB target draining, AWS case open. Postmortem assigned. :white_check_mark:
Kevin: Thanks team. Add customer impact summary (latency, error budgets, affected endpoints) to postmortem and coordinate comms with ops-communications. :thumbsup:
